hypothesis: Reproduce the official FM baseline through this pipeline before proposing anything.
rationale: Every later delta is measured against this number. If the pipeline cannot reproduce 0.6016 the harness is wrong and no subsequent result means anything.
expected_gain_derivation: Not an improvement attempt; a correctness precondition. Target validation primary 0.6016.
note: seeds best-so-far and the convergence window; does not start the stall counter

hypothesis: Replacing the pointwise FM with LightGBM trained with lambdarank on ~6-row training groups, over base5 plus out-of-fold item aggregates and within-user duration features, will lift validation primary well above 0.6016.
rationale: Three structural mismatches in the baseline are addressed by mechanisms that are known to bite here: (a) the loss is pointwise while the metric is a within-user ordering metric, so lambdarank's pairwise gradients optimise exactly the quantity scored [POINTWISE_BASELINE]; (b) training groups average 43.5 rows while scored lists average 5.6, so capping groups at 6 consecutive rows makes the training position discount and pair sampling match the evaluation list geometry [GROUP_SHAPE_MISMATCH][SHORT_EVAL_LISTS]; (c) an FM must infer item quality from a sparse embedding per video, whereas an OOF-encoded video/author long-view rate hands the tree a dense, directly within-user-varying quality signal, and 99.9% of valid videos are covered by the train window [HIGH_COVERAGE]. Duration features add the duration-bias axis the organizers flag as unexplored and vary within a user's list, unlike user-side aggregates.
expected_gain_derivation: The organizers measured static fields and capacity as dead [ORGANIZER_FEATURES_DEAD][ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD] but list loss function and duration bias as untouched [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED], which locates the remaining headroom in the loss/geometry/dense-signal axis rather than in more embedding. Headroom is large: 0.8484 perfect vs 0.6016 baseline [CEILING], i.e. ~0.247 available, and switching from a pointwise sparse-embedding model to a GBDT with dense OOF item rates plus a list-matched ranking loss typically recovers a fifth to a quarter of such a gap on tabular impression logs; 0.22 x 0.247 ~ 0.055. This is far above the 0.0008 seed-noise floor [SEED_NOISE], so the sign should be unambiguous.

block_justifications.base5: Reference field set; video_id, author_id, tab and dur_bucket all vary within a single user's impression list so they can actually reorder it [WITHIN_USER_RANKING], and it keeps this spec comparable to the 0.6016 baseline.
block_justifications.item_agg: OOF video/author long-view and click rates are dense item-quality signals that differ between the ~6 rows of a user's list, and 99.9% valid-video coverage means they are populated at eval time [HIGH_COVERAGE].
block_justifications.dur_feats: long_view is mechanically duration-dependent and the within-user duration percentile is by construction non-constant across a user's rows, addressing the duration-bias direction the organizers left unexplored [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED].

hypothesis: Dropping the base5 ID categoricals and training LightGBM-lambdarank on ~6-row groups over only out-of-fold item aggregates and within-user duration features will lift validation primary well above the 0.6021 obtained when those IDs were present.
rationale: Inside a user's list, user_id is literally constant so it can only act as a memorisation split that lets the tree fit per-user offsets on the 43-row training lists, and video_id/author_id at thousands of levels with max_cat_threshold=64 gives LightGBM an enormous overfitting surface that crowds out the dense, genuinely discriminative signals. item_agg (OOF video/author long-view and click rates) and dur_feats (log duration, within-user duration percentile) both vary row-to-row inside a user's list and are exactly the quantities that can reorder it; with the IDs removed the split budget goes entirely to them.
expected_gain_derivation: Iteration 1 bundled base5 with item_agg+dur_feats and returned 0.60209, only +0.0007 over the FM baseline and barely outside seed noise [SEED_NOISE]. Since [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT] says user_id contributes exactly zero orderable information, its only possible effect is variance/overfit, and [ORGANIZER_CAPACITY_DEAD] shows this dataset does not support extra memorisation capacity. If the dense item-quality plus duration signals are worth anything at all, they should be visible once the ID splits stop absorbing them; I put the recoverable amount at roughly a quarter of the way from 0.602 to a realistic 0.65 tree ceiling, hence +0.014, with real downside risk if base5 was in fact carrying video-quality signal that item_agg duplicates only weakly.

hypothesis: Adding the cross_agg block (user x author affinity, user x tag affinity, duration relative to the user's own historically long-viewed duration) to the iteration-1 LightGBM lambdarank spec will lift validation primary well past 0.6034.
rationale: Iteration 2 showed that removing the ID fields costs 0.018, i.e. essentially all of the model's signal lives in the user-item interaction that the FM absorbs through its user_id x video_id embedding dot product; a tree cannot reconstruct that interaction from two high-cardinality categoricals. cross_agg supplies exactly that interaction in a dense, tree-splittable numeric form (this user's historical affinity for this author / these tags), and unlike user_agg it varies row-to-row inside a user's list so it can actually reorder it. It is the only untried block that encodes personalisation rather than global item quality, and it is a single-block delta on a spec whose score I already know, so attribution stays clean.
expected_gain_derivation: [USER_CONSTANT_NO_EFFECT] plus the iteration-2 result bound the size: dropping IDs (the only user-personalised information in that spec) cost 0.0179, so the personalised component of the signal is worth at least ~0.018 of primary. cross_agg should recover that component more efficiently than raw IDs do in a tree, but not all of it, and part of it is already captured by base5 in iteration 1's 0.6021. I therefore take roughly 70% of 0.018 as the ceiling and halve it for overlap with base5, giving ~+0.013 over 0.6021 (~0.615). [SEED_NOISE] says the measurement resolves anything above 0.0008, and [CONVERGENCE_MECHANICS] requires >0.6034, which this comfortably clears if the mechanism is real.

block_justifications.base5: Iteration 2 measured that removing these IDs costs 0.018 primary, so they are load-bearing and must stay for this to be a clean one-block delta on the 0.6021 spec.
block_justifications.item_agg: Held fixed from the 0.6021 reference spec so the only change is cross_agg; OOF item long-view rates vary across the ~6 rows of a valid list and 99.9% of valid videos appear in train [HIGH_COVERAGE].
block_justifications.dur_feats: Held fixed from the reference spec; within-user duration percentile is non-constant across a user's rows by construction and addresses the duration-bias direction [ORGANIZER_UNEXPLORED].
block_justifications.cross_agg: The one change under test: user x author and user x tag affinity is the user-item interaction term that iteration 2 proved carries the signal, expressed as dense numerics a tree can split on rather than as high-cardinality IDs.
